## Interpretation

### Background

The parent panel ([#560](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/560), MODERATE) found that the broad-negative marker recipe carries a universal side effect: every one of 557 off-source (adapter, persona) cells gets a positive end-token logit push, with personas the training never mentioned averaging **+13.66** — slightly MORE than the trained negatives (+12.46). That killed the exposure account ("the clamp goes where the negatives were") but explicitly left the cause unidentified. The older 4-negative lineage ([#553](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/553)/[#478](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/478)) had shown a near-zero held-out clamp (~−3.1) under a different recipe, suggesting panel composition as the prime suspect. This experiment is the registered causal ablation: train four fresh adapters identical in everything except the negative panel, and read the clamp on 32 personas neither panel ever mentioned.

### What was run

Two arms x two seeds, single source context (software-engineer persona prompt), the i474 recipe held fixed: the broad arm reproduces the exact 15-context x 20-row negative panel; the narrow arm uses a 4-context class-spanning subset ({plain assistant, query-wrap, bare chat template, register rephrase} — one per context class, always including the default assistant) at 75 rows each, total negatives fixed at 300 in both arms. Honest bundling note carried from the plan: at fixed total, shrinking the panel necessarily raises per-bystander rows (20→75) and question coverage — "panel composition" is the registered manipuland; "breadth per se" is not isolated. Eval reused the parent's four-float on-policy surface unchanged (35 personas x 20 questions, greedy, slot read trained-vs-base on the same text).

### Results

**1. The registered verdict is `confirmed`: panel composition causes most of the universal end-of-answer clamp.** Shrinking the panel from 15 contexts to 4 (rows fixed) drops the never-mentioned-persona end-token push from **+15.35 to +5.93** logits — a paired contrast of **+9.43** [+8.58, +10.28] (n = 32 personas), positive for every single persona, with the manipulation check passing on all four adapters and the broad seed-42 cell replicating the parent's measured value to within 0.03 logits. Both matched-seed contrasts are positive (+6.70 / +12.15), the gauge-invariant companion agrees, and restricting to slot-kind-matched cells makes the contrast larger (+12.73), not smaller. The broad panel's breadth-side composition is causally responsible for roughly 60% of the clamp at this dose.

**2. The narrow panel does NOT reproduce the old 4-negative lineage's near-zero clamp — and it buys the weaker clamp at the cost of near-universal marker hijack.** The narrow arm still clamps held-out personas by ~+6 logits (vs the lineage's −3.1 qualitative anchor, measured under a different recipe/cap), so composition explains most but not all of the side effect. More striking: narrow-arm adapters emit the marker on **92-96%** of held-out answers and loop it to the 2,048-token cap on 88-93% — vs 15-18% emission for broad — with the never-negative emission margin at **+16.8** logits (narrow) vs **+2.0** (broad). The internal control is clean: trained negatives never emit (assistant 0/20 everywhere; comedian/villain 0/20 only where trained). So the two recipes sit on a trade-off: broad suppression panels buy marker containment and pay with a universal "end your answer" push; narrow panels avoid most of the push and let the implant hijack nearly everyone. Neither side effect is free.

**3. Magnitudes are less settled than signs.** The narrow-arm level is seed-sensitive (+8.11 vs +3.74 never-neg mean across the 2 seeds), and the registered Confirmed-vs-Partial boundary (narrow < +7) is cleared by the pooled mean (+5.93) but violated by seed 42 alone. The CAUSAL direction (composition modulates the clamp, large positive contrast) is robust to every diagnostic run; the absolute narrow-arm level and the exact contrast magnitude carry 2-seed uncertainty.

### Main takeaways

- Panel composition is established as a causal lever behind the universal end-of-answer clamp: a 15-context suppression panel teaches "end your answer" to everyone at ~2.6x the strength of a 4-context panel with the same number of suppression rows.
- The exposure story's replacement is now concrete: broad suppression generalizes the EOS push beyond its training targets, while per-context suppression itself works perfectly where trained (0/20 emission on every trained negative, both arms).
- A pre-training audit pricing the recipe's side effects has to price BOTH channels: broad panels → universal clamp; narrow panels → near-universal off-target marker hijack. Composition choices move side effects between channels rather than eliminating them.

### Confidence: MODERATE

The registered confirmatory verdict fired with zero caps, the contrast is large, persona-unanimous (32/32), sign-stable across seeds, DV spaces, and slot restrictions, and the replication anchor pinned rig identity to 0.03 logits. Held below HIGH by: 2 seeds per arm with a 4.4-logit narrow-arm seed spread (the narrow < +7 confirm conjunct fails on seed 42 alone and is carried by the pooled rule); a single source context (A2); and the bundled manipulation — panel breadth co-varies with per-bystander row count (20→75) and question coverage at fixed total, so the causal claim is scoped to panel composition, not breadth per se.

### Proposed title

`Negative-panel composition causes most of the universal end-of-answer clamp: a 4-context panel clamps never-mentioned personas at well under half the 15-context push (MODERATE confidence)`

(Second finding — the narrow panel's near-universal marker hijack — goes to the TL;DR and its own finding H4, not the title.)

## Interpretation

### Background

The parent panel ([#560](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/560), MODERATE) found that the broad-negative marker recipe carries a universal side effect: every one of 557 off-source (adapter, persona) cells gets a positive end-token logit push, with personas the training never mentioned averaging **+13.66** — slightly MORE than the trained negatives (+12.46). That killed the exposure account ("the clamp goes where the negatives were") but explicitly left the cause unidentified. The older 4-negative lineage ([#553](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/553)/[#478](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/478)) had shown a near-zero held-out clamp (~−3.1) under a different recipe, suggesting panel composition as the prime suspect. This experiment is the registered causal ablation: train four fresh adapters identical in everything except the negative panel, and read the clamp on 32 personas neither panel ever mentioned.

### What was run

Two arms x two seeds, single source context (software-engineer persona prompt), the i474 recipe held fixed: the broad arm reproduces the exact 15-context x 20-row negative panel; the narrow arm uses a 4-context class-spanning subset ({plain assistant, query-wrap, bare chat template, register rephrase} — one per context class, always including the default assistant) at 75 rows each, total negatives fixed at 300 in both arms. Honest bundling note carried from the plan: at fixed total, shrinking the panel necessarily raises per-bystander rows (20→75) and question coverage — "panel composition" is the registered manipuland; "breadth per se" is not isolated. Eval reused the parent's four-float on-policy surface unchanged (35 personas x 20 questions, greedy, slot read trained-vs-base on the same text).

### Results

**1. The registered verdict is `confirmed`: panel composition causes most of the universal end-of-answer clamp.** Shrinking the panel from 15 contexts to 4 (rows fixed) drops the never-mentioned-persona end-token push from **+15.35 to +5.93** logits — a paired contrast of **+9.43** [+8.58, +10.28] (n = 32 personas), positive for every single persona, with the manipulation check passing on all four adapters and the broad seed-42 cell replicating the parent's measured value to within 0.03 logits. Both matched-seed contrasts are positive (+6.70 / +12.15) and the gauge-invariant companion agrees. An exploratory end-of-response-only subset read points the same way (+12.73, larger not smaller), but that subset is sparse and non-random — 6 personas selected precisely because the narrow arm left them any end-of-response slots, i.e. the least-hijacked personas — so the slot-mix confound is reduced, not discharged. The directly supported causal claim: the bundled fixed-total panel-composition manipulation (15 contexts x 20 rows vs 4 contexts x 75 rows) produces a **+9.43-logit reduction** in the never-mentioned-persona end-token push.

**2. The narrow panel does NOT reproduce the old 4-negative lineage's near-zero clamp — and it buys the weaker clamp at the cost of near-universal marker hijack.** The narrow arm still raises the EOS logit on held-out personas by ~+6 (vs the lineage's −3.1 qualitative anchor, measured under a different recipe/cap), so panel composition explains most but not all of the side effect. More striking: narrow-arm adapters emit the marker on **92-96%** of held-out answers and loop it to the 2,048-token cap on 88-93% — vs 15-18% emission for broad — with the never-negative emission margin at **+16.8** logits (narrow) vs **+2.0** (broad). Neither pattern is uniform: narrow's non-firings concentrate in a small resistant set (`formal_assistant` 0/20 in BOTH narrow seeds; `grumpy_person`, `sarcastic_assistant`, `overly_enthusiastic_assistant`, `serious_comedian`, `open_mic_comedian` carry the rest, mostly in seed 42), and broad's firings concentrate in the close engineering personas (`devops_engineer`, `machine_learning_engineer`, `web_developer` 20/20 in both broad seeds; medical personas high but seed-sensitive). The internal control is clean: trained negatives never emit (assistant 0/20 everywhere; comedian/villain 0/20 only where trained). And the parent's key dissociation (#560's F2) replicates WITHIN both arms: behavioral suppression is perfectly trained-target-specific (0/20 emission wherever a context was trained as a negative, in both arms), while the EOS-logit clamp shows no exposure gradient at all — trained negatives and never-mentioned personas get clamped at the same level (broad +13.82 vs +15.35; narrow's one realized trained negative +6.81 vs +5.93, n = 1 descriptive). So the two recipes sit on a trade-off: broad suppression panels buy marker containment and pay with an across-the-board positive EOS-logit push on held-out personas; narrow panels avoid most of the push and let the implant hijack nearly everyone. Neither side effect is free.

**3. Magnitudes and mechanism are less settled than signs.** The narrow-arm level is seed-sensitive (+8.11 vs +3.74 never-neg mean across the 2 seeds), and the registered Confirmed-vs-Partial boundary (narrow < +7) is cleared by the pooled mean (+5.93) but violated by seed 42 alone. One confound is ruled out by direction: the narrow arm implants the marker somewhat HARDER on source (Δz_marker 29.51/27.83 vs broad's 25.05/25.71, asymmetry 3.29 — below the 5-logit cap) yet clamps held-outs LESS, so "narrow clamps less because it implanted less" fails on sign, not just on the cap. A residual mechanistic alternative stays open: the narrow arm's much larger held-out marker margin (+16.8 vs +2.0) and near-ceiling emission could mechanically relate to its lower EOS push (marker/EOS competition at the slot), so the strongest causal sentences here stay scoped to the bundled panel-composition manipulation. The CAUSAL direction (panel composition modulates the clamp, large positive contrast) is robust to every diagnostic run; the absolute narrow-arm level and the exact contrast magnitude carry 2-seed uncertainty.

### Main takeaways

- Panel composition is established as a causal lever behind the universal end-of-answer clamp: under the bundled fixed-total manipulation, the 15-context panel raises the end-token (EOS) logit on all 32 never-negative held-out personas at ~2.6x the strength of the 4-context panel (+15.35 vs +5.93), with the same number of suppression rows.
- The exposure story's replacement is now concrete: broad suppression generalizes the EOS push beyond its training targets, while per-context suppression itself works perfectly where trained (0/20 emission on every trained negative, both arms) — and the no-exposure-gradient dissociation reproduces within both panels.
- A pre-training audit pricing the recipe's side effects has to price BOTH channels: broad panels → across-the-board EOS-logit push on held-out personas; narrow panels → near-universal off-target marker hijack. Composition choices move side effects between channels rather than eliminating them.

### Confidence: MODERATE

The registered confirmatory verdict fired with zero caps, the contrast is large, persona-unanimous (32/32), sign-stable across seeds and DV spaces, and the replication anchor pinned rig identity to 0.03 logits. Held below HIGH by: 2 seeds per arm with a 4.4-logit narrow-arm seed spread (the narrow < +7 confirm conjunct fails on seed 42 alone and is carried by the pooled rule); a single source context (A2); the bundled manipulation — panel breadth co-varies with per-bystander row count (20→75) and question coverage at fixed total, so the causal claim is scoped to panel composition, not breadth per se; and a cross-arm slot-kind mix difference (narrow slots ~92% pre-marker vs ~15% for broad) that the sparse end-of-response-only subset read reduces but does not discharge.

### Proposed title

`Negative-panel composition causes most of the universal end-of-answer clamp: a 4-context panel clamps never-mentioned personas at well under half the 15-context push (MODERATE confidence)`

(Second finding — the narrow panel's near-universal marker hijack — goes to the TL;DR and its own finding H4, not the title.)

### Next steps

- Decompose the bundle: hold per-bystander rows fixed (4 contexts x 20 rows = 80 total, or 15 x 75 = 1,125 total) so panel COUNT separates from rows-per-context and coverage. (cost_class: needs-gpu, headline_affecting: no)
- Add 2-3 seeds per arm to pin the narrow-arm absolute level against the +7 Confirmed/Partial boundary. (cost_class: needs-gpu, headline_affecting: yes — could demote `confirmed` to `partial`; requires fresh training, not free)
- Replicate on a second source context (a query-wrap or register-rephrase source) to test generality beyond A2. (cost_class: needs-gpu, headline_affecting: no)
- Geometry read of the contrast: correlate the per-persona contrast with #560's A2 cosine distances (data already committed). Exploratory mechanism color only. (cost_class: free-analysis, headline_affecting: no)

**Free-analysis follow-ups (orchestrator: auto-run before parking): none qualify** — the only free-analysis item (geometry read of the contrast) is not headline-affecting; every headline-affecting follow-up needs new GPU training. `free_analysis_unrun: []`.

### 1. Un-bundle the panel-composition manipulation: add the two missing factorial cells (4 contexts × 20 rows; 15 contexts × 75 rows) — Type: Ablation

**Parent:** #571
**question_relation:** same

**Hypothesis:** Context COUNT, not rows-per-context, carries the clamp. The parent's per-context suppression loss hits 0.00 by end of epoch 1 at BOTH 20 and 75 rows/context (extra rows are redundant gradient), and the push is exposure-blind — so spreading suppression over many distinct contexts is what generalizes "end your answer" to everyone.
